subject: Acme: analytics/data-use carveout - proposed redline & Product/Security review
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elena.torres@acmecorp.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@acmecorp.com>
Date: 2026-10-18T09:12:00-04:00
Subject: Request: data-use carveout for analytics / telemetry (DPA redlines attached)

Hi Rishi,

Thanks for the quick demo last week. Legal here — attaching our proposed DPA redlines. The primary ask is a carveout that would allow Acme to permit aggregated analytics on inferred telemetry that includes KV-cache-derived metadata and anonymized prompts for model performance analysis. Our counsel is pushing to retain aggregated snapshots for 90 days to support debugging and product analytics.

Key asks in the redline (Acme_DPA_redlines_v1.pdf attached):
- Allow "analytics telemetry" derived from session KV snapshots (aggregated/non-personally-identifiable).
- Retention of aggregated telemetry up to 90 days.
- Right to export raw snapshots to our S3 for debugging in limited cases (customer-initiated).

We understand Redwood's privacy stance; please advise if these items are acceptable or if Product/Security will need to propose alternatives. We need a response for our procurement timeline (targeting a signature by 10/28).

Thanks,
Elena Torres
Senior Counsel, Acme Corp
elena.torres@acmecorp.com
Attachment: Acme_DPA_redlines_v1.pdf
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@acmecorp.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-18T11:05:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Request: data-use carveout for analytics / telemetry (DPA redlines attached)

Elena — thanks for sending this over and for the clarity in the redlines. Looping in Laura (Legal/Security) and Dev (Product) to confirm feasibility and controls.

Short response: we want to be helpful to Acme's analytics needs, but we need Product/Security to confirm what the runtime actually persists, what can be exported, and whether we can agree to the 90-day retention on aggregated data.

Action items for our side:
- Laura: can you review the attached PDF and call out specific terms that trigger escalation?
- Dev: can you confirm whether KV cache snapshots are ever persisted by default, whether there is an opt-in export path, and what encryption/controls apply?

I captured a quick internal summary for context for Product/Security (internal_summary.md attached).

If we can propose an equivalent safe route (e.g., aggregated-only telemetry with short retention and customer-initiated raw export), we should present that to Acme as a compromise.

Rishi
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, Elena Torres <elena.torres@acmecorp.com>
Cc: dev_patel@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-19T08:30:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Request: data-use carveout for analytics / telemetry (DPA redlines attached)

Thanks Rishi and Elena — reviewed the PDF. High level: Acme's proposed retention and the ability to export raw snapshots are the two items that require explicit Security sign-off (and likely a customer-controlled export constraint).

Proposed secure alternative language (to discuss internally before we send to Acme):
"Customer may export session-related artifacts (including KV cache snapshots) only via an explicit, documented export operation initiated and authenticated by the Customer. Exported artifacts will be encrypted in transit and at rest and delivered to Customer-managed storage. Aggregated telemetry intended for product analytics will be non-identifiable and retained for no more than 30 days unless Customer requests otherwise in writing."

Notes and open Qs for Product/Security:
- Is 30 days a hard requirement? Would 14 days be preferable operationally?
- Can we guarantee that default product behavior never persists raw KV snapshots outside ephemeral memory?
- If we permit customer-initiated exports, what audit logging and access controls will we commit to in the DPA?

I've attached a short proposed language file (prop_lang_suggestion.txt). Dev — can you fill in the technical guarantees (ephemeral vs persisted cache) and confirm whether encryption and delivery to customer storage are supported today.

Laura
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference
Attachment: prop_lang_suggestion.txt
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: Elena Torres <elena.torres@acmecorp.com>, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-19T14:45:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Request: data-use carveout for analytics / telemetry (DPA redlines attached)

Laura / Rishi / Elena — quick product/engineering note: runtime behavior today
- KV cache is maintained in GPU/host memory for inference performance and is ephemeral by default; we do not persist raw KV snapshots to long-term storage as part of normal serving.
- We do have an export mechanism used for debugging where a customer can trigger an export; in Dedicated/Private deployments exports can be delivered to customer-managed S3 or object store. For Hosted customers we can provide encrypted export artifacts via a signed URL or push to a customer AWS account via cross-account role (requires setup).
- Aggregated telemetry can be emitted from runtime (counts, latency histograms, token distributions) and we can avoid including prompt text or PII. That data is configurable — default retention is 14 days in our telemetry pipeline, extendable with approval.

Operational safeguards we can commit to:
- Exports require explicit customer action and are logged (time, initiating user/email, export id).
- Export artifacts are AES-256 encrypted and can be delivered to customer-managed storage.
- We can redact prompt text from aggregated telemetry; including anonymized metrics derived from KV metadata is feasible.

Suggested contract language to accept with modifications: state that raw snapshot export is permitted only if customer-initiated and delivered to customer-managed encrypted storage; aggregated telemetry retention capped at 30 days by default (we can offer 14 days as the platform default), and any longer retention requires written approval from Redwood Security.

Attaching a screenshot that shows export flow in the console for reference (screenshot_runtime_kv.png). Happy to jump on a short call if needed.

— Dev
Principal Product Manager, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
Attachment: screenshot_runtime_kv.png
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@acmecorp.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-20T09:10:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Request: data-use carveout for analytics / telemetry (DPA redlines attached)

Elena — thank you and sorry for the slightly longer thread. Summary / next steps from Redwood: 

1) Product confirms runtime is ephemeral by default and raw KV snapshots are not persisted unless a customer explicitly initiates an export.
2) Security/legal propose we accept an export carveout that meets these conditions: customer-initiated export only; direct delivery to customer-managed encrypted storage; export operations are auditable and logged.
3) Aggregated telemetry: Redwood can provide non-identifiable, aggregated metrics. Platform default retention = 14 days; we can offer 30 days with Security approval. Any retention >30 days requires written approval and will be considered on a case-by-case basis.

If Acme is agreeable to the above controls, Laura will circulate final DPA language reflecting the export constraints and retention caps; we will then route to Procurement for signature.

Please confirm whether Acme can accept: (a) export-to-customer-storage only (no hosted raw retention by Redwood), and (b) 30 days maximum without special approval. If yes, I will ask Procurement to kick off the amendment and Hannah will prepare a short Security audit note for Acme’s records (security_audit_note.docx attached).

Thanks — Rishi
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
